how_navigation_actually_works.verified_by: reading templates/macros/sidebar.html, templates/partials/sidebar.html, templates/partials/topnav.html, templates/macros/breadcrumb.html, templates/macros/page-navigation.html, templates/page.html, tools/generate-section-tree.mjs, tools/_regen_nav.mjs, tools/generate-relkey-map.mjs, tools/generate-section-indexes.mjs, data/navigation.json, data/section-tree.json
how_navigation_actually_works.version_dropdown: templates/partials/topnav.html iterates nav.meta.versions; every entry needs nav.routes['/<version>/<lang>/'] (label comes from there) and data/relkey_map.json for the same-relkey target
how_navigation_actually_works.sidebar: templates/macros/sidebar.html (called by templates/partials/sidebar.html) renders ONLY routes whose node.parent == '/vX/lang/' AND whose node.group matches a key of nav.groups; children come from node.children (curated, copied from section-tree subsections) and from section-tree.byRoute[...].subsections
how_navigation_actually_works.breadcrumb: templates/macros/breadcrumb.html uses Zola item.ancestors, i.e. it needs a real _index.md at every ancestor level; the navigation.json fallback branch needs nav.routes entries
how_navigation_actually_works.parent_and_prev_next: templates/macros/page-navigation.html reads Zola parent_section.pages; it needs an _index.md in the section and works out of the box once the page exists. Ordering is Zola's default (site-wide no frontmatter weight is used today)
how_navigation_actually_works.generated_not_handwritten: data/section-tree.json is fully generated from content/ by tools/generate-section-tree.mjs; data/navigation.json routes are generated by tools/_regen_nav.mjs from that tree and PRESERVE label/group from existing entries; data/relkey_map.json is generated by tools/generate-relkey-map.mjs from a hard-coded VERSIONS list

patches.why: Zola breadcrumb for every v1.4.6 page walks page.ancestors: v1.4.6 -> v1.4.6/zh -> v1.4.6/zh/architecture. get_section(path='v1.4.6') returns nothing without this file, so the breadcrumb link 404s on every single v1.4.6 page. It is also what nav.routes['/v1.4.6/'] needs in order to exist.
patches.risk: none - file did not exist before

patches.why: The version dropdown and the sidebar root_key computation both gate on nav.meta.versions. Without v1.4.6 here, every v1.4.6 URL falls back to the 'Site Navigation' branch of the sidebar and the version dropdown never lists v1.4.6.
patches.note: _regen_nav.mjs copies existing.meta verbatim, so this edit survives regeneration.

patches.why: The file is generated from content/. tools/audit-navigation.mjs fails with 'missing section route /v1.4.6/...' until it is regenerated. Never hand-edit it.
Creates the /v1.4.6/... routes with correct parent/children from the section tree.

follow_up.problem: For brand-new routes _regen_nav.mjs sets group = ex?.group ?? null, i.e. null. templates/macros/sidebar.html only renders a route when node.parent == root_key AND node.group == group_key, so every v1.4.6 route with group null stays invisible in the sidebar (v1.4.5 has the same nulls on leaf routes, which is harmless because leaves are rendered through their parent's children list).
follow_up.mirror_of: exactly what v1.4.5 already carries: group 'start' for the three roots, 'api' for <lang>/api/, 'architecture' for <lang>/architecture/, 'guide' / 'native' / 'xml' for the other sections

patches.risk: medium - easy to forget the group, symptom is 'sidebar shows nothing for v1.4.6'

patches.why: data/relkey_map.json maps a relkey to every version/lang that has that page. Without v1.4.6 in VERSIONS the version dropdown falls back to /v1.4.6/<lang>/ (version landing) for every page, so switching version from a class page throws you back to the landing page instead of the equivalent page.

patches.why: The hand-written version table is the site-level version picker. The BEGIN/END SECTION INDEX block below it is machine generated and will pick up /v1.4.6/ on its own once the table row exists.

No change needed. The macro derives root_key from nav.meta.versions and renders whatever groups/labels navigation.json provides; once P1+P3 are applied v1.4.6 appears with the same behaviour as v1.4.5. Adding a version must not require a template change - that is the whole point of the data-driven sidebar.
Pure dispatcher (imports macros/sidebar.html and calls render_nav with current_url/lang). Nothing version specific.

Every dropdown loops over nav.meta.versions and gates on nav.routes[route_key] being defined, then links via get_url('@/<version>/<lang>/<section>/_index.md'). No version is hard-coded except the v1.3.15 native-source entry, which is intentionally version specific.

Driven by Zola page.ancestors + get_section(), so it works as soon as every ancestor level has a real _index.md. That is what P0 guarantees. Its navigation.json fallback branch also works once P1+P3 land.

Parent link and prev/next siblings are computed from Zola parent_section.pages at render time, i.e. automatically bidirectional as soon as the page and its section _index.md exist. Do not hand-write prev/next into pages.

No version list, no per-version menu, no redirect table. [slugify] paths = "off" already preserves the api/<module-slug>/ directory names this version relies on, taxonomies are empty, so a new version needs no config change. If a per-version warning banner is ever wanted that is a separate feature, not a navigation patch.

patches.replace: add "  '1.4.6':  'bannerlord-1.4.6'," to ROOTS (and extend the two hard-coded ['1.3.0','1.3.15','1.4.5'] output loops if a 1.4.6 column is wanted)
patches.why: Without it, tools/class-version-diff.mjs cannot produce a 1.4.6 column, which is why version-delta.md had to state that signature-level deltas are not verified.

pending_link_policy.why: api/ sections and class pages are produced by a parallel worker. Links from worker-10 pages into content/v1.4.6/{zh,en}/api/** were written before those files existed and were declared pending up front.
pending_link_policy.not_allowed_missing: everything else, including cross-version links into v1.3.15 / v1.4.5 / versions/
pending_link_policy.status_at_handover: 0 pending. All 23 api module sections referenced below exist and resolve. Re-run node tools/_v146_nav-check.mjs after the api batch changes; if it prints OWNED_LINKS_PENDING > 0, that batch renamed or dropped a section and the module-map table must follow.

link_depth_rule.rule: On an _index.md page (route = its own directory) children are ./child or child/; on a leaf page (route = <dir>/<page>/) siblings are ../child. Never use more ../ than the page's own route depth.
link_depth_rule.why: tools/audit-links.mjs builds routes WITHOUT a leading slash (fileToRoute returns dir + '/'), so an over-deep ../../.. escapes the content root and is reported as BROKEN even though a browser resolves it correctly. Found while authoring: content/v1.4.6/zh/_index.md had ../../../versions/ (route depth 2) and the audit flagged it; rewritten as ../../versions/.
link_depth_rule.audit_tool_caveat: audit-links is the stricter gate and disagrees with the browser on over-deep relative paths. Treat its verdict as authoritative for this repo.
